findings.message: `waived_edges` は `plan_fulfillment_record` にしか適用されません。Waiver と同じ edge の `VoluntaryBinding` はこの owner ループで Fulfillment action を生成し続けるため、check gate の waiver precedence と不一致になり、不要な二重 adjudication と誤った tally/cache を生じます。

この変更で 1 件の voluntary binding が複数 owner 分の Fulfillment action を生成する一方、calibration の production-pair 数は voluntary binding を 1 件として数えます。そのため複数 owner のケースでは実際の adjudication 数より少ない calibration probe しか発行されず、検出率ゲートが過少評価されます。

`ProviderSessionCacheError` exposes filesystem/codec mechanics (`Io`, `Symlink`, `Path`, `Codec`) through the usecase port. This makes callers aware of adapter implementation details and allows infrastructure errors to leak across the abstraction boundary. Replace these with usecase-level cache failure concepts and map filesystem-specific causes inside the infrastructure adapter.

`plan_binding_records` decides the domain-level precedence rule that a waiver suppresses fulfillment and voluntary bindings. This duplicates the same rule from the check gate, allowing evaluators to diverge when the rule changes. Move precedence/mutual-exclusivity resolution onto the domain binding model and let the usecase orchestrate the resolved outcome, per `hexagonal-architecture.md` §CLI as Composition Root.

The usecase defines edge ownership by comparing an obligation's entry key and spec references. That relationship is a domain predicate, and duplicating it here (including the existing single-owner variant) risks inconsistent ownership semantics across check/evaluate flows. Expose this through `TestObligation` or `ObligationsDocument` in domain and consume it from the orchestrator, per `hexagonal-architecture.md` §CLI as Composition Root.

T006 is a split candidate. Its infrastructure work alone includes the evaluator (~1,265 changed lines), codec (~344), adapter (~149), schema exporter, verification/render changes, and tests—already multiple times the configured 500-line per-scope ceiling before the usecase and composition work is counted. Split T006 into independently reviewable tasks.

T006 attributes the action:`modify` `RustdocSchemaExporter` entry, but its description never targets either `libs/infrastructure/src/schema_export.rs` or `RustdocSchemaExporter`. This is not a reference-entry carrier attribution: add that target and operation to T006 so the task contract matches the executable task boundary.

T006 is not review-sized. Its infrastructure work alone spans roughly 1,974 changed lines across the named files—almost 4× the configured 500-line ceiling—and `type_signals_evaluator.rs` alone exceeds twice the ceiling. Describing six retrospective sub-scopes without separate task IDs does not make them independently committable; split T006 into actual tasks.

T006 sub-scopes (e) and (f) are stale against their attributed contracts. They describe a fallible declaration-digest boundary, place `LoadCatalogueSpecSignalsForViewError` under `infrastructure::verify::catalogue_spec_signals`, and associate `RustdocSchemaExporter` with that boundary. The attributed catalogue contracts instead make both hash functions infallible, locate the error in `type_catalogue_render`, and modify `RustdocSchemaExporter` for `existing_rustdoc_json_path`. An executor must invent the correct target and operation; update these sub-scopes to match the task-contract attributions.
`plan.summary` still maps GO-03 and GO-04 to the removed T006 and omits replacement tasks T010–T015, leaving goal-to-task traceability stale. Replace T006 with the applicable split task IDs.

T011 is mapped to AC-08 even though it only adds usecase ports, orchestration, and errors; it contains no artifact schema, encoding, decoding, or legacy-artifact validation step. Remove the AC-08 mapping or add executable work that actually covers it.

Those mappings are not supported by T015's described work or task-contract entries.

findings.message: CN-08 requires a new-session fallback when the capability resume cache cannot be read or hashed, but no AC covers those cases. AC-09 covers valid entries and profile/contract mismatch, while AC-10 covers resume failure and expiry; an implementation could omit read/hash-failure fallback and still satisfy every AC.

findings.message: GO-04 promises preservation of review judgment and review-record semantics, but no acceptance criterion deterministically verifies that session resume leaves the judgment/record unit unchanged. AC-03 verifies full-scope rejudgment only, and AC-04 verifies session selection and flag injection; both could pass while resumed rounds alter record semantics.
findings.category: missing AC coverage for a stated goal

findings.message: AC-05 permits signal-evaluation skip whenever the implementation, catalogue, baseline, and evaluator hashes match, even when the rustdoc-extraction contract changed or the live snapshot cannot be verified. CN-07 and AC-07 require rustdoc extraction and recalculation in those same cases, so the contract simultaneously permits skipping and requires recomputation, risking stale signals. The skip condition must also account for the extraction contract and snapshot-validity requirements.

AC-09 applies its resume requirement to any `sotp capability exec` invocation carrying the resume option, but that command also has an in-host delegation outcome. This requires cache-backed resume for the in-host branch that OS-05 explicitly excludes. Restrict this criterion to provider-subprocess dispatches or explicitly specify that in-host dispatch rejects/ignores resume.

GO-03 requires every evaluation whose decision inputs changed to run, but AC-05's complete-skip predicate omits the spec/catalogue↔spec input, and AC-06/AC-07 provide no spec-change path. A spec-only change could therefore satisfy the stated skip conditions and leave catalogue↔spec signals stale, contrary to D3. GO-03 lacks deterministic acceptance coverage for this case.
findings.category: missing AC coverage for a stated goal

findings.message: CN-08 and AC-09 require invalidation on a capability execution-contract fingerprint mismatch, but the spec never defines that fingerprint's inputs for generic capability resume; IN-04 defines only the reviewer-specific fingerprint. D4 identifies capability SSoT, always-injected discipline, and declared policy/contract files as inputs. Without an equivalent contract here, downstream phases must invent which changes invalidate the cache, making stale-reuse prevention untestable.

IN-08 requires a fresh session when the concern changes, even if the target artifact remains the same. However, AC-09 only checks the resume option and track/capability/artifact identity, so all acceptance criteria can pass while a same-artifact concern switch incorrectly resumes stale context. This leaves GO-02/GO-04 without deterministic coverage for a prohibited reuse path.

findings.message: AC-05 の第1文は declaration_hash の一致も rustdoc 抽出を skip する必要条件にしていますが、同じ AC の第3文と AC-06 は、implementation-side input hash が一致して declaration_hash だけが不一致の場合にも rustdoc を起動しないと定めています。同一状態に対して相反する routing となるため、rustdoc 抽出の要否は implementation-side input hash のみに基づき、declaration/spec の差分は signal 再評価の要否だけを決める契約に統一する必要があります。

The ReasoningEffort waiver is justified by Batch A scheduling and future tasks (T003/T007), not by an entry-local reason why this type cannot cover CN-02. This leaves the waiver dependent on implementation sequencing; replace it with an entry-surface argument, as done for CapabilityProfile, or bind the behavior to a real test.

This waiver cites the plan task `T007` and a specific test to justify the waiver. The briefing requires waiver reasons to argue only from the entry's declared surface, with no task IDs or scheduling language. Rewrite the rationale solely in terms of `FsProviderSessionCacheAdapter`'s observable API and limitations.

This waiver assigns the behavior to plan task `T007`, directly violating the requirement that waiver reasons contain no task IDs and rely only on the entry's declared surface. Explain only why `ProviderSessionCacheEntry` cannot represent or perform the AC-10 behavior.

The regenerated obligations add 19 enforced `logic_result` obligations for `ObligationsDocument`, `TestBindingsDocument`, and `TestObligation`, but none has a fulfillment or waiver in `test-bindings.json`. Consequently, `bin/sotp test-obligation check --track-id agent-dispatch-cost-reduction-2026-07-13` fails with `Missing` drifts. Add bindings and regenerate the caches before committing these obligations.

The `method:staleness_against` fulfillment is bound only to edge-ownership and evaluation-fan-out tests; none invokes `ObligationsDocument::staleness_against`. Consequently the generated cache marks both associated edges fulfilled using unrelated assertions, so the obligation gate can remain green without evidence for this method. Bind the existing staleness tests instead and regenerate the cache.

Eleven voluntary-binding records contain duplicate TestLocation entries. SignalCompositionRoot repeats the same test seven times for IN-06, IN-07, CN-07, and AC-05 through AC-08; TypeSignalsDocument/IN-05 and both RustdocSchemaExporter edges repeat it twice; TypeSignalsReuseDecision/IN-05 repeats it three times. The evaluator concatenates every listed test body without deduplication, so these records inject 47 redundant test-body copies into verifier prompts, overweight a single test, and produce duplicate-sensitive `bound_tests_set_hash` values. Deduplicate each record and regenerate the fulfillment cache.

The fulfillment for `ObligationsDocument::track_id` binds only edge-ownership and evaluator tests; none calls `track_id()`. The existing `test_obligations_document_round_trips` test does exercise this accessor but is not bound, so the obligation is incorrectly reported as fulfilled.

The fulfillment for `TestBindingsDocument::track_id` binds waiver/evaluator tests that never call `track_id()`. Bind `test_bindings_document_round_trips`, which actually verifies this accessor, so the gate cannot pass on unrelated evidence.

The fulfillments for `TestObligation::{target_entry,target_role,brief,declaration_hash}` all cite the same ownership/evaluator tests, none of which invokes these accessors. `test_obligation_exposes_all_components` exercises all four but is absent, causing four public-API obligations to be marked fulfilled without relevant evidence.

The `ClaudeReviewer` contract-conformance fulfillment still does not bind `test_claude_reviewer_resumes_only_matching_track_scope_and_round_key_unit`. The bound static-cache tests do not prove IN-03's track/scope/round isolation or fast-to-final fresh-session behavior; binding that test only to AC-03/AC-04 cannot support the separate IN-03 verdict. Add it to this fulfillment and regenerate the cache.

The `ReviewCompositionRoot` bindings for CN-02, CN-03, and CN-09 still contain only infrastructure reviewer unit tests. None execute `ReviewCompositionRoot`, so regressions in its flag/profile wiring, current-scope propagation, or review-record persistence would leave these entry-specific edges fulfilled. Bind composition-level evidence for each edge and regenerate the cache.

`test-bindings.json` has changed again beyond the previously reviewed T004 append (the new diff adds evidence tests for ReviewCompositionRoot IN-04/CN-02/CN-03/CN-09), but `obligation-fulfillment-cache.json` is unchanged for those records. Because each cache entry stores `bound_tests_set_hash`, the cached frozen verdicts are stale relative to the current bindings and the machine artifacts are internally inconsistent; regenerate the cache after the binding update.

The resolved `effort` is discarded here, and `run_dry_fix_codex` consequently launches Codex without `model_reasoning_effort`. Even though missing effort now fails during profile resolution, every successful `dry-fix-lead` dispatch still falls back to Codex's implicit default, violating the explicit/fail-closed effort contract. Capture the effort and pass it into the Codex invocation.

The shared ref/obligation verifier runner discards the resolved `effort`. The Codex branch continues to hardcode `high`, so configured fast=`low` and final=`xhigh` executions both run at the wrong level; Claude/Gemini likewise receive no resolved effort. Thread the typed effort into each provider's argument builder instead of using a hardcoded or provider-default value.

For out-of-host Claude dispatches, the resolved `request.profile.effort` is dropped: `build_claude_args` receives only capability, model, and prompt, so no `--effort` flag reaches the subprocess. An explicitly configured effort therefore silently falls back to Claude's provider default, violating D1's fail-closed execution contract.

Codex generic dispatch similarly ignores `request.profile.effort`; the generated arguments contain model and sandbox but no `model_reasoning_effort` override. Capabilities resolved through `AgentProfilesCapabilityAdapter` consequently run with Codex's implicit default despite having a validated explicit effort.

The baseline is hashed before its symlink guard runs. Because `SkipEvaluation` returns before the later guard, a symlinked baseline outside `canonical_items` can participate in a successful freshness match. Run `reject_symlinks_below(&baseline_path, &canonical_items)` before `hash_identity`.

The persisted signal artifact is read without checking the leaf or its ancestors for symlinks. A valid schema-v2 document reached through a symlink can supply the recorded hashes and trigger `SkipEvaluation`. Apply the established `reject_symlinks_below` guard before reading it.

Both contract fingerprints hash only `type_signals_evaluator.rs`. Evaluator behavior also depends on `signal_evaluator_v2`, `signal_tags`, codecs and rules, while extraction behavior depends on `schema_export`, target/root resolution, invocation arguments, features, and configuration. Changes to those inputs leave these hashes unchanged and can incorrectly reuse stale signals or snapshots. Hash the complete resolved closures required by ADR D3.

The build-input fingerprint treats every local package closure as fully resolved after hashing its package tree, but it neither discovers build-script inputs outside that tree nor rejects custom-build packages whose inputs cannot be determined. For example, changing a workspace-level schema named by `cargo:rerun-if-changed` can alter generated public API while this hash remains unchanged, allowing a stale snapshot reuse. Detect unresolved build-script inputs and fail closed, or include their resolved files/tools in the hash.

The new reuse path loads both existing rustdoc snapshots and persisted signal artifacts with unbounded `read_to_string` calls. A malformed large file can exhaust memory before parsing; the existing signal reader already establishes a 16 MiB bounded-read pattern. Enforce explicit size limits before these reads.

The evaluator/extraction fingerprints hash files from the runtime source checkout identified by the compile-time `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, rather than the code embedded in the running `bin/sotp`. If source B is evaluated with an older binary A, that binary writes results produced by A while recording B's hash; after installing binary B, the hashes match and evaluation can be skipped, leaving stale signals. Exported/transplanted binaries can also reference a nonexistent build-host path. Embed a build-time contract digest in the binary instead of reading mutable source files at runtime.

`encode` serializes the document's arbitrary schema version even though this codec only supports the current version. Because `TypeSignalsDocument::with_schema_version` is public, callers can emit a schema-v3 file with the schema-v2 shape which this codec immediately rejects on read. Validate the version before serialization or always emit `TYPE_SIGNALS_SCHEMA_VERSION`.

Cargo configuration files are detected with `is_file()` and loaded with `std::fs::read`, both of which follow symlinks. This bypasses the repository's real-file config convention and can read configuration outside the intended config root. Use `symlink_metadata()` and reject symlinks before loading, following the `scope_config_loader.rs` pattern.

The common build-input reader follows symlinks for workspace/package manifests and `Cargo.lock`; unlike the source traversal, it performs no `symlink_metadata().file_type().is_symlink()` rejection. A symlinked freshness input can therefore escape the trusted workspace boundary. Reject symlinks before every `append_file` read.

The build-input closure recursively enumerates every regular file under each local package and then reads each file fully into memory without any file-count, depth, per-file-size, or aggregate-byte bound. A large generated file or sufficiently large tree can exhaust memory or make the mandatory review prelude effectively unbounded. Apply explicit traversal and byte limits and fail closed when exceeded.

The workspace-root symlink check occurs only later in the evaluation, after this call has already executed `cargo metadata` and traversed manifests and source files beneath `workspace_root`. Because leaf `symlink_metadata` checks follow symlinked ancestors, a symlinked workspace root reaches external I/O before rejection. Validate the workspace anchor before any freshness hashing or snapshot resolution.

Build scripts are rejected only for local/path packages. Registry or git dependencies with `custom-build` targets remain reusable even though their outputs can depend on untracked system files; changing such an input can alter rustdoc output without changing this digest. Reject unresolved build scripts across the complete dependency closure or hash their resolved inputs/outputs.

The source collector unconditionally excludes package-root `tmp` and every directory named `target`, without proving they are build outputs. Cargo permits declared sources such as `[lib] path = "tmp/lib.rs"`, so changing that source produces the same implementation-input hash and can incorrectly reuse stale signals. Derive the source closure from Cargo inputs or fail closed when an excluded directory is referenced.

The snapshot-reuse method uses `resolve_target_dir`, whose metadata failure or malformed output silently falls back to `<workspace>/target`. A transient resolution failure can therefore select and verify an old snapshot at the default path instead of forcing rustdoc extraction, contrary to the conservative freshness contract. Use a strict target-directory resolver for reuse that propagates any metadata/parse failure.

The freshness hash records environment-variable strings and the fixed `rustup run nightly rustc -Vv` output, but not the identity/content of the actual compiler or documentation executable selected by Cargo (`RUSTDOC`, `CARGO_BUILD_RUSTDOC`/`build.rustdoc`, `RUSTC`, or wrappers). If a custom rustdoc binary changes in place at the same path, the implementation-input hash remains unchanged and `SkipEvaluation` can reuse stale output. Hash the resolved executable identity/content or treat such overrides as indeterminate and re-extract.

`collect_contract_files` recursively traverses contract-source directories and accumulates paths without any depth, file-count, or aggregate-byte bound. The per-file limit is applied only afterward, so a sufficiently deep or large source tree can exhaust stack, memory, or build time. Add fail-closed traversal budgets like those in `build_inputs::collect_package_files`.

`implementation_input_hash` には target 名または path 文字列だけが入り、custom target JSON の内容が含まれません。同じ path の target specification を変更しても hash が変わらず、古い rustdoc snapshot に対して `SkipEvaluation` が選ばれ得ます。custom target の内容も hash 化するか、解決不能として再利用を拒否してください。

評価後に baseline と workspace inputs を再読込して freshness hash を作っていますが、評価前の値との一致を確認していません。長い rustdoc 実行中に source、lockfile、baseline が変更されると、旧入力で生成した signals/snapshot と新入力の hash が同じ artifact に保存され、次回は誤って `SkipEvaluation` できます。評価に使用した同一 bytes の hash を保持するか、前後の hash が一致しなければ再試行または失敗させてください。

The traversal budget counts only regular files. Directories consume no budget, so a package tree containing arbitrarily many empty directories (within the depth limit) causes unbounded `read_dir` recursion during signal freshness calculation. Count every visited directory entry or add a global directory/entry limit.

The build-script traversal has the same unbounded-directory gap: `ContractSourceBudget.files` increases only for files, allowing arbitrarily many empty directories to bypass all count and byte limits and exhaust build time/resources. Apply a bounded total-entry or directory count before recursing.

An absolute `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` with a symlinked ancestor is accepted. For example, with `/tmp/link -> /outside`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/link/target` causes `symlink_metadata()` to follow `link` and inspect only the real leaf directory. Later checks treat that lexical target as the trusted root and inspect only descendants, so snapshot reuse can read `/outside/target/doc/*.json`. Reject every target-directory component with the existing ancestor-walking symlink guard before trusting it.

`reject_symlinked_type_signals_anchor` checks only the final path component. A `workspace_root` or `items_dir` reached through a symlinked parent passes this check; subsequent canonicalization resolves both paths through the link, so containment also passes. The freshness pipeline can consequently read build inputs and write signals outside the intended lexical workspace. Use the existing `reject_symlinks_up_to_root` pattern, consistent with the repository's symlink-parent rejection tests.

`append_local_package_sources` only hashes files beneath each package directory. Rust inputs can legally escape that directory through `include!`, `include_str!`, `include_bytes!`, or `#[path]`; changing such a shared file leaves `implementation_input_hash` unchanged and can incorrectly select `SkipEvaluation`, accepting stale type signals. Hash compiler-reported external inputs or fail closed when the complete closure cannot be established.

The new freshness commands use `Command::output()`, which buffers unbounded stdout and stderr before any source-closure byte budget applies. `cargo metadata` can contain arbitrarily large manifest metadata/dependency output, so this path can exhaust memory before failing closed; the rustup commands have the same issue. Stream subprocess output through explicit size limits.

Strict snapshot target resolution buffers the complete `cargo metadata --no-deps` stdout/stderr via `Command::output()` without a bound. Large workspace/package metadata can therefore exhaust memory during snapshot lookup. Read the subprocess pipes with a fixed cap and reject over-limit output.

The evaluator and extraction contract digests are built from hand-picked infrastructure paths. Semantics from local path dependencies and helpers outside these lists can change without changing Cargo.lock or the hashed manifests, leaving the contract hash unchanged and permitting stale reuse. Hash the complete resolved code/build closure required by D3/CN-05.

Local package hashing walks only the manifest's parent directory and ignores Cargo metadata's `targets[].src_path`. A valid target path outside that directory can therefore change without affecting `implementation_input_hash`, allowing stale rustdoc snapshots to be reused. Hash every resolved target source root or reject targets escaping the package root.

The bounded-output helper limits retained bytes but has no wall-clock timeout: `child.wait()` and the pipe readers can block forever if cargo, rustup, or a descendant never exits or retains a pipe. These calls run in the reviewer prelude, so one stuck subprocess can hang the review indefinitely. Add bounded waiting and process-tree termination.

`cargo metadata`-derived `manifest_path` values are read and recursively traversed without proving that each package root remains under `workspace_root` or another explicitly trusted root. A repository-controlled external path dependency can therefore make freshness calculation enumerate and hash files outside the repository. Apply an `is_safe_briefing_path`-style validation, canonical containment check, and ancestor-symlink rejection; per CN-04, roots that cannot be authorized must fail closed into re-extraction.

The new snapshot lookup calls `resolve_rustdoc_root_name`, whose `cargo metadata` subprocess uses unbounded `.output()`. This puts the freshness path at risk of an indefinite subprocess or unbounded stdout/stderr allocation before the bounded metadata lookup runs. Use the bounded command runner with an output cap and timeout.

`core_source_roots` enumerates `libs_root` and grows `roots` without applying the declared entry budget. The later recursive scan is bounded, but a workspace with many direct library entries can consume unbounded time and memory before that budget is created. Apply an entry limit during this top-level scan as well.

The freshness closure rejects unresolved `custom-build` targets but accepts `proc-macro` targets. Procedural macros can perform arbitrary filesystem I/O while generating the rustdoc-visible API; changing such an external file would not change any currently hashed field, allowing stale `SkipEvaluation`. Reject unresolved proc-macro targets or include a verified hermetic input identity.

The byte scanner can miss valid external-input syntax such as `include /* comment */ !("../../shared.rs")` and `#[cfg_attr(feature = "x", path = "../../shared.rs")]`. Those referenced files lie outside the walked package tree, so their contents can change without changing `implementation_input_hash`, permitting stale snapshot reuse. Use syntax-aware detection or otherwise fail closed for unresolved source inputs.
`items_dir` is no longer canonicalized and checked beneath `workspace_root`; the subsequent `join` reads and writes arbitrary paths outside the trusted workspace.
Catalogue, baseline, signal, and track paths are read without `reject_symlinks_below`; symlinked files can redirect I/O outside `items_dir`. Restore the existing boundary checks.

Source traversal uses `is_dir`/`is_file` and `fs::read`, which follow symlinks. A source symlink can hash external content or recurse through a directory loop, violating the exact-input and fail-closed requirements.
`canonicalize()` resolves `repo_root` before the symlink check, so a symlinked repository root is accepted and cache writes can target the resolved location instead of the configured trusted root.
Existing rustdoc JSON is only checked for bounded UTF-8 text; malformed JSON is passed to evaluation and returns an error instead of taking the required re-extraction path.

Implementation-input hashing performs unbounded recursive directory traversal and `fs::read` calls after the previous file/count/depth budgets were removed, allowing resource exhaustion instead of fail-closed rejection.
The rustup identity subprocess uses raw `Command::output()` without an output limit or timeout, so a hung or excessively verbose toolchain command can block or exhaust memory.

`symlink_metadata(&source_root)` checks only the final `src` component. A symlinked `libs` or crate directory is followed by `read_dir`, allowing source files outside the trusted workspace to be hashed.

The implementation hash includes `target_crate` as an extra semantic input, although the contract specifies exactly source contents, `Cargo.lock`, and nightly toolchain identity. This causes hash drift when only the target label changes.

`read_regular_source_file` now passes every source file and `Cargo.lock` directly to `std::fs::read` without a per-file or cumulative byte limit. The file-count/depth caps do not prevent a single large or sparse input from causing an arbitrarily large allocation and resource exhaustion during review. Restore pre-read size checks, a cumulative byte budget, and a post-read race check; exceeding them should make the hash indeterminate and fail closed.

`canonical_repo_root` checks only the final path component before canonicalization. If an ancestor is a symlink, canonicalization can redirect the cache root outside the supplied repository, allowing reads/writes there. Reject symlinks through all ancestors before canonicalizing.
`fs::read` は事前のサイズ確認後にファイルが拡大すると、上限を超えて無制限に割り当てる可能性があります。bounded reader と post-read 上限検証を使用してください。

`execute_with_dependencies` reads the catalogue with unbounded `std::fs::read`, and `verify_evaluation_inputs_unchanged` repeats the same unbounded read. An oversized track catalogue can therefore cause arbitrary allocation before decoding. Use a bounded regular-file reader such as `File::take(limit + 1)` for both reads.

`save` does not enforce `MAX_CACHE_ENTRY_BYTES`, although `load` rejects entries above that limit. Because session IDs, provider/model names, and workspace artifact identities have no size bound, the adapter can write a cache entry it cannot subsequently load while also allocating and writing without a bound. Reject oversized encoded entries before opening the file and add a boundary test.

`MAX_SOURCE_FILES` only counts regular files, while every directory is recursively traversed without any total directory/entry budget. A `src/` tree containing arbitrarily many empty directories can therefore make implementation-input hashing perform unbounded filesystem work despite the advertised traversal cap. Count every visited entry (or add a separate directory budget) and fail closed when the bound is exceeded.

The re-extraction path discards the pre-launch implementation hash and replaces it only after rustdoc finishes. If source files, Cargo.lock, or the nightly toolchain change during extraction, the resulting rustdoc JSON can represent the old or mixed inputs while the persisted document records the new post-extraction hash. The later unchanged-input check only brackets evaluation, so a subsequent run can incorrectly skip evaluation. When the initial hash was available, compare it with the post-extraction hash and fail or retry on mismatch while retaining the explicit transient-unavailable recovery path.

The new Codex stdout collector accumulates the entire `--json` event stream in one `String` for the duration of the reviewer subprocess. A verbose or malfunctioning child can therefore cause unbounded heap growth and OOM before the timeout; the previous implementation continuously drained and discarded this stream. Capture only a bounded `thread_id` event while continuing to drain subsequent output.

Claude stdout is now bounded, but stderr is still accumulated without limit in a `String`. A noisy or malfunctioning reviewer child can exhaust the parent process heap before the timeout; cap retained stderr bytes while continuing to drain the pipe.

The authoritative `--output-last-message` file is read with unbounded `read_to_string`. A malformed reviewer subprocess can create an arbitrarily large file and exhaust memory during verdict loading; enforce a maximum size and fail closed on overflow.

Codex stderr is streamed into a persistent session-log file without any byte limit. A verbose or malfunctioning child can exhaust workspace disk before the timeout; retain a bounded log while continuing to drain stderr.

`drain_pipe` discards stdout via `BufRead::lines()`, which allocates until a newline is found. A malfunctioning child can emit an arbitrarily long newline-free record and exhaust heap memory even though the content is discarded. Drain fixed-size byte chunks instead.

The authoritative verdict file is opened without rejecting symlinks. The file can be replaced after initialization and before this read, redirecting verdict parsing to another file. Enforce real-file semantics with the same explicit `symlink_metadata().file_type().is_symlink()` rejection used by `scope_config_loader.rs` before opening the file.

D3 の入力 hash は source 内容・Cargo.lock・toolchain 識別子 בלבדで、Cargo.toml の feature/target 設定、rustflags/RUSTDOCFLAGS、その他 rustdoc 出力を変える設定を捕捉することが明示されていません。この変更後も hash が一致して signal 再計算を skip すると、古い type-signals を新しい実装条件に対して再利用できます。実装が hash に含める入力集合と、未モデル化入力時の fail-closed 動作を決定として明記してください。

D4 は継続作業を「同じ成果物」への再入に限定していますが、track cache のキーは track × capability だけで対象 artifact を含みません。同一 track 内で同じ capability が別 artifact を扱うと、orchestrator が resume を opt-in した際に前の artifact の session を再利用し、stale context を引き継げます。track cache も artifact/work-unit identity をキーまたは検証条件に含める必要があります。
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: D3 simultaneously requires skipping signal recalculation when implementation inputs are unchanged and re-evaluating when the catalogue/spec changes, but it does not define a retained and validated rustdoc snapshot for that re-evaluation. The downstream implementation cannot safely evaluate a changed catalogue without rerunning rustdoc or specifying a cache, so this can consume absent/stale data.

The D3 freshness hash does not explicitly cover all inputs that affect the stored signals: the evaluator also consumes the baseline rustdoc artifact, and rustdoc/evaluation can vary with path-dependency, build-script, or proc-macro source changes not captured by the listed target-crate source and lockfile inputs. Without an explicit complete input closure or fail-closed detection for these cases, an unchanged hash can incorrectly skip recalculation and leave stale signals.

D3 is internally inconsistent: it says baseline changes may reuse the live rustdoc snapshot without extraction (lines 54–56), but then requires the current baseline hash to equal the artifact’s recorded baseline hash. Any actual baseline change makes that condition false and forces rustdoc recomputation, so downstream implementation cannot derive the stated skip behavior.
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: D2 lists `fresh-every-round` as a rejected candidate, but no Rejected Alternatives entry actually rejects fresh reviewer sessions. H concerns capability dispatches under D4, while C only rejects cross-tier resume, leaving D2's reviewer-session choice without a corresponding rationale.
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: D3 requires skipping rustdoc extraction and later reusing a verified live snapshot, but it only specifies storing the snapshot hash in the type-signals artifact while explicitly rejecting a separate transient cache. It does not define where the snapshot body is persisted or how it is loaded; regenerating it with Cargo would perform the extraction that D3 intends to skip, while omitting it makes signal recomputation impossible. Downstream implementation/spec cannot derive a working acceptance criterion for this reuse path.

D2/D4 の session cache は provider/model だけで再利用可否を決め、review briefing・severity policy・capability contract の世代変更を無効化または再注入する規則がありません。再起動後や規約更新後に同じ track/scope/artifact で resume すると、古い判断規則・作業契約のまま review/編集を続け得るため、observable な fail-closed 条件を追加してください。

D1 の candidate_selection にある `merge-fast-final-tiers` は、Rejected Alternatives A-L または採択 decision に対応する説明がありません。fast/final の effort tier を統合する案を却下したのか、採択方針に含めるのかが decision trace から判定できず、ADR の選択理由と downstream acceptance criteria の根拠が不完全です。
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: D2 fingerprints the contents of the resolved scope files and generated briefing, then invalidates the session on any mismatch. A fixer re-round necessarily changes at least a scoped file—and the briefing may also be regenerated—so the cache always falls back to a new session instead of resuming as D2 requires. Separate stable execution-contract inputs from mutable review inputs.
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: D4 includes the dispatch briefing's contents in the fingerprint and invalidates the session when they change. Since `capability exec` receives each task through that briefing, follow-up or repair work normally requires changing it; the intended continuation therefore becomes a fresh session. The decision must specify which stable contract portion is fingerprinted independently of the changing task payload.
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: D3 permits skipping signal evaluation when “all inputs” are unchanged, but the defined freshness state covers only the target rustdoc build-input closure, catalogue declaration, baseline, and snapshot. Signal results also depend on the evaluator implementation and its configuration, which can change without changing any of those hashes; downstream spec.json therefore cannot derive an observable invalidation rule, and previously generated signals may remain stale after evaluation semantics change. Specify how the evaluation contract participates in freshness or when reevaluation is mandatory.

D3 は evaluator-contract の変更時にも既存 rustdoc snapshot の再利用を許可していますが、その contract 自体に evaluator 実装の code/build identity を含めています。抽出用の引数・root 解決・JSON 生成方法を担う実装が変わっても、実装側 input hash と旧 snapshot の自己 hash が一致すれば旧 snapshot を再利用できるため、「判定不能なら rustdoc 抽出から再計算する」という fail-closed 方針に反して stale signal を生成し得ます。下流 spec が安全な再利用条件を導出できるよう、抽出結果へ影響する contract の変更を snapshot 無効化条件として明確にしてください。
findings.category: inconsistent decisions within the same ADR

findings.message: The dry-checker final/default effort is set to `high`, but D1 requires reviewer-like final lanes on Codex to use the provider maximum, `xhigh`. The final DRY-check lane therefore runs below the required effort level; set `reasoning_effort` to `xhigh`.

`dry-checker` の fast/final 用キーが契約と異なります。`reasoning_effort` ではなく `final_reasoning_effort: "xhigh"` が必要で、現在の `fast_reasoning_effort: "medium"` も D1 の fast=low に違反します。このままでは final dispatch が必須 effort を解決できず fail-closed で失敗します。

`review_operational` excludes only the fulfillment half of the test-obligation verdict-cache pair. `bin/sotp test-obligation evaluate` persists both `obligation-fulfillment-cache.json` and `waiver-cache.json`, and the workflow explicitly treats both as generated frozen-verdict outputs. Because `waiver-cache.json` still classifies as `other`, any evaluation that refreshes a waiver verdict changes the reviewed `other` hash and recreates the evaluate → stale → re-review loop this change is intended to eliminate. Add `track/items/<track-id>/waiver-cache.json` to `review_operational` as well.

`Resume(Vec::new())` and other invalid target sets now return a rendered error and skip dispatch, but the briefing explicitly defines this case as an intentional fail-closed degradation to `ResumeWithoutTarget`. This changes the required resume behavior and can abort otherwise valid capability execution.

`Sha256Digest`, `TypeSignalsFreshness`, and `TypeSignalsSchemaVersion` are private-field value objects with no declared constructor or accessors, so the infrastructure codec/evaluator cannot create or inspect the freshness data required by `TypeSignalsDocument`.

`ProviderSessionCacheEntry` is opaque (`has_stripped_fields: true`) but declares no constructor, accessors, or serialization boundary. The cache port returns and accepts this type, leaving adapters and provider callers unable to persist or validate its session/profile/fingerprint fields.

`TargetArtifactPath` and `TargetArtifactSet` are private-field value objects with no construction or read API, while `CapabilityResumeArg` crosses from CLI-driver into these types. The declared boundary has no way to convert validated CLI paths into the usecase resume identity.

`FsProviderSessionCacheAdapter` and `Sha256ExecutionContractFingerprintAdapter` both have private state and empty method declarations, including no `new`/factory method or `Default` impl. The composition root therefore cannot construct either adapter for the dependencies it claims to wire.

`ExecutionContractFingerprintPort::reviewer_fingerprint` and `capability_fingerprint` return `ProviderSessionCacheError`, whose `Io`, `Symlink`, and `Path` variants are structurally unrelated to the declared pure fingerprint operations. The entry does not document a justified subset; callers must handle unreachable cache-storage failures.

`ProviderSessionCachePort` is explicitly a machine-local persistence port, but all `load`/`save`/`remove` methods are synchronous and the entry does not acknowledge the blocking-I/O choice. This fixes the adapter contract to blocking filesystem operations without documenting the color decision.

`TypeSignalsExecutorPort::evaluate_layer` takes filesystem roots and a layer binding and delegates semantic evaluation/rustdoc execution, yet is declared synchronous with no documented sync-I/O decision. The port contract leaves the adapter's external-process/filesystem execution model underspecified.

The `CapabilityDispatchOutcome` docs restate the upstream resume-boundary contract and the `Executed` payload semantics (including why raw `u8` is opaque) instead of only citing the `IN-08`/`OS-05` anchors.

The `ProviderSessionCacheEntry` docs restate profile/fingerprint compatibility and expiry fallback behavior from the upstream contract; this behavior must remain in the cited spec anchors rather than being duplicated in the type catalogue.
The `AgentProfiles` docs restate the upstream routing invariant that `provider_label` is display-only and must not be used as identity, rather than referring to the `IN-01`/`IN-02`/`CN-01` anchors.
The `AgentProfilesError` docs restate the upstream diagnostic-data policy for `UnsupportedSchemaVersion` instead of limiting the catalogue entry to the type change plus its anchors.

`cli::CapabilityExecArgs` declares only capability, host, briefing_file, and timeout_seconds, while `cli_driver::CapabilityExecDriverInput` requires `resume: CapabilityResumeArg`. The resume selector and target artifacts are therefore unreachable from the CLI, so the IN-08/AC-09 resume flow cannot be invoked.

`TypeSignalsExecutorPort` abstracts blocking rustdoc/filesystem work and is consumed by `TypeSignalsInteractor`, so it is an application-service port rather than a domain concept. Declaring it as a `SecondaryPort` in the domain catalogue violates the Port Placement Rules; move this contract (and its executor error surface) to the usecase layer and have the infrastructure adapter implement that port.

`TypeSignalsInteractor` is marked `action: modify`, but its declared public shape and constructor are identical to the rustdoc baseline; only its implementation behavior is planned to change. This makes Chain ③ blue before the implementation lands and contradicts the catalogue's modify semantics. Mark it `reference` or omit it if no type-level edge requires it.

Several baseline-identical entries are incorrectly marked `modify`: `AgentProfilesCapabilityAdapter`, `TypeSignalsExecutorAdapter`, `infrastructure::tddd::type_signals_codec::decode`, and `...::encode`. Their declared constructors/signatures contain no post-track structural delta, so they already evaluate blue before implementation. Use `reference` or omit body-only changes from the type catalogue.

`CapabilityDriver` is marked `action: modify`, but its declared public methods match the baseline exactly; the planned resume validation is a method-body change. Representing it as `modify` falsely claims a post-track structural change and allows Chain ③ to be blue before that behavior exists. Use `reference` or omit the entry.

`CapabilityCompositionRoot` is marked `action: modify`, although its declared public constructor and accessor signatures match the baseline. Changes to stripped private wiring do not constitute a catalogue-visible shape delta, so this should be `reference` rather than an already-blue `modify`.

Both `cli::commands::capability::execute` and `cli::commands::review::execute` are marked `action: modify`, but their parameter and return signatures are baseline-identical; only their bodies will change. Mark these entries `reference` or omit them so the catalogue does not claim unenforceable structural modifications.

`domain::tddd::type_signals_doc::decide_type_signals_reuse` requires a complete `current: &TypeSignalsFreshness`, including `LiveRustdocSnapshotHash`, even when `snapshot_status` is `Missing` or `ReadFailed`, where no current snapshot hash exists. Callers must fabricate a hash, and the separate parameters also admit contradictory states such as `Verified` paired with an unrelated hash. Carry the verified hash in the status enum or separate current input hashes from recorded freshness.

The new `TargetArtifactPath::try_new`, `TargetArtifactSet::try_new`, `ProviderSessionId::try_new`, and `ReviewerPrompt::try_new` methods all return the seven-variant `CapabilityInputValidationError`, although each can produce only a small, disjoint subset. Their declarations neither document those subsets nor justify the broad error surface, forcing callers to handle structurally impossible variants.

`CapabilityResumeArg::into_domain` returns the full `CapabilityInputValidationError`, but only conversion of `Resume(Vec<TargetArtifactPathArg>)` can fail, specifically while constructing `TargetArtifactSet`; provider, model, file-path, content, and timeout variants are structurally unreachable. Declare or document the producible subset.

`AgentProfiles::resolve_execution` operates on an already-loaded profile yet returns `AgentProfilesError`, exposing loader-only variants such as `Io`, `Symlink`, `PathOutsideTrustedRoot`, `Parse`, and `UnsupportedSchemaVersion`. Its declaration does not document a producible subset or justify requiring resolution callers to handle these impossible failures.

`infrastructure::tddd::type_signals_codec::encode` accepts an already validated `TypeSignalsDocument` but returns the shared `TypeSignalsCodecError`, including decode-only validation failures such as `InvalidSchemaVersion`, `InvalidTimestamp`, and `InvalidDigest`. The method does not identify its producible subset or justify this broad surface.

`ExecutionContractFingerprintPort` は reviewer 専用の `reviewer_fingerprint` と capability 専用の `capability_fingerprint` を単一 interface に束ねています。`CodexReviewer` / `ClaudeReviewer` と capability adapter 群の利用系統は分離しており、各 mock・代替実装に無関係なメソッドの実装を強制します。reviewer 用と capability 用の SecondaryPort に分割してください。

`ExecutionContractFingerprintPort` の両メソッドは guarded contract file を読み取る外部 I/O 境界ですが、いずれも同期メソッドであり、docs は blocking I/O を同期 dispatch path で行う設計判断を説明していません。同期を意図するなら bounded blocking の選択を明記し、そうでなければ async 境界にしてください。

`ProviderSessionCachePort::remove` は共有 `ProviderSessionCacheError` を返すため `Codec` まで公開しますが、key による削除処理は entry の encode/decode を行わず、この variant を構造的に生成できません。`ExecutionContractFingerprintPort` と同様に生成可能な subset を method docs で限定するか、より精密な error type を使用してください。

`infrastructure::ref_verify::process_runner::build_gemini_ref_verifier_args` returns the six-variant `usecase::ref_verify::RefVerifyError`, although this function can only construct `VerifierPort`. Its docs neither declare that producible subset nor justify the broad error surface, forcing callers to account for structurally impossible variants.

The `build_gemini_ref_verifier_args` docs restate the upstream fail-closed behavior and its rationale (“because Gemini cannot accept invocation-scoped typed effort”) instead of limiting the catalogue description to the symbol’s purpose plus the existing IN-01/IN-02/CN-01 anchor citations, contrary to `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`LoadCatalogueSpecSignalsForViewError::Hash` is dead vocabulary. Both sources of `Sha256DigestError` are already canonical: `declaration_hash` formats a SHA-256 value as exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, while the loader revalidates `ContentHash::to_hex()`, which has the same guarantee. Consequently neither `InvalidLength` nor `InvalidHex` can occur. The fallible contracts on `infrastructure::tddd::type_signals_codec::declaration_hash` and `infrastructure::verify::catalogue_spec_signals::compute_catalogue_declaration_hash` propagate an impossible failure and create this unconstructible variant. Provide an infallible conversion for computed digest bytes and reserve fallible parsing for external strings.
findings.category: unconstructible error variant / per-method error imprecision

findings.message: `RustdocSchemaExporter::existing_rustdoc_json_path` returns the broad `domain::schema::SchemaExportError`, but this method neither checks nightly, launches rustdoc, nor parses rustdoc JSON. Its implementation maps its resolution and path-safety failures exclusively to `RustdocFailed`, leaving `NightlyNotFound`, `ParseFailed`, and `CrateNotFound` structurally unreachable. The catalogue docs neither list that producible subset nor justify the broad error. Declare a method-specific error or explicitly narrow the contract.

The `infrastructure::RustdocSchemaExporter` docs restate AC-06's behavioral contract by promising verified snapshot resolution without launching rustdoc. Under `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`, catalogue docs should identify the changed symbol and cite the upstream anchors rather than duplicate their behavior; replace this clause with an anchor-only change description such as adding `existing_rustdoc_json_path` for IN-06/AC-06.

The `decide_type_signals_reuse` docs restate the CN-07/AC-07 fail-closed behavior (“an unavailable implementation input hash forces re-extraction”) instead of limiting the entry to the symbol and anchor references.

The `ProviderSessionCacheEntry` docs restate the upstream provider/model compatibility and resume flag-injection contract. Keep that behavior in the cited spec anchors and describe only the type change here.
`ImplementationInputHash` の docs は CN-05 の source/lockfile/toolchain 入力契約を散文で再記述しています。上流アンカー参照と型の変更対象だけに絞ってください。
`domain::SchemaExporter` と `usecase::SchemaExporterPort` は rustdoc/process・filesystem I/O を行う同期ポートですが、docs が blocking synchronous design を明記していません。同期境界を意図するならその選択を契約に記載してください。
`TypeSignalsInteractor` は rustdoc baseline と同じ公開 shape・constructor なのに `action: modify` です。変更は実装本体のみで、catalogue-visible な型変更を宣言していないため `reference` にしてください。

`usecase::ProviderSessionCacheKey::TrackCapability` still includes `target_artifacts`, but IN-09/AC-09 and restored ADR D4 define the track-local key as track × capability; target-artifact identity applies only to workspace-local caching. This retains the rejected mechanical invalidation behavior, so changing the target set within the same track/capability incorrectly selects another cache entry and prevents the intended resume. Remove `target_artifacts` from `TrackCapability` while retaining it on `WorkspaceCapability`.

`usecase::ProviderSessionCacheKey` restates the complete session-keying behavior from IN-03/IN-09/CN-04/AC-03/AC-09 in `docs`. Replace this behavioral restatement with a short type-purpose phrase and anchor citations, as required by `knowledge/conventions/no-upstream-restatement.md`.

`domain::ObligationsDocument::owning_obligation` returns `Option<&TestObligation>`, while the same contract introduces `owners_of_edge` and AC-11 permits multiple obligations to own one edge. `None` therefore conflates “no owner” with “multiple owners,” allowing consumers to silently skip required per-(edge × obligation) handling. Remove the singular API or return a type that distinguishes no, unique, and multiple owners.

`cli_driver::CapabilityResumeArg::Resume` carries a plain `Vec<TargetArtifactPathArg>`, so the public driver API admits `Resume(vec![])` alongside the separate `ResumeWithoutTarget` state. This bypasses the usecase mirror’s non-empty `TargetArtifactSet` invariant and allows an empty targeted resume to be treated as targetless rather than rejected, potentially selecting a track-scoped cached session. Use a non-empty validated payload or fallible construction so this overlapping state is unrepresentable.
